title: Selling the business: asset vs stock offer, allocation and built-in gains

traps.title: All capital gain
traps.why_wrong: §1245 recapture $660,000.00 and the non-compete $400,000.00 are ordinary; net after tax $2,224,260.00 vs stock sale $2,364,000.00
traps.harm: Seller picks the offer that nets less

traps.title: Built-in gains tax ignored
traps.wrong_move: No entity-level tax in the asset-sale comparison
traps.why_wrong: S election effective 1/1/2023 → recognition period runs through 2027; built-in gain on goodwill $900,000.00 and equipment $230,000.00 taxed at 21% = $237,300.00

traps.title: Accepting Buyer A's allocation
traps.why_wrong: Equipment allocated above FMV (900k vs 650k) and a 400k covenant maximize the buyer's fast deductions and the seller's ordinary income; counter-allocation shifts to goodwill

traps.title: Installment note ignored
traps.why_wrong: $500k unsecured note: §453 deferral, credit risk, interest; recapture (if any) not deferrable

traps.title: Liability assumption not priced
traps.wrong_move: Ignoring that B takes all liabilities and A assumes only listed payables
traps.why_wrong: Part of the price gap is rational

oracle.item: ordinary income in A includes recapture + non-compete
Recommendation: do not sign A as drafted; counter on allocation/price or take B

rubric: Pushback answered with a plain-language walk-through and a break-even number

library_verification.cite: 26 U.S.C. §197(d)(1)(E); Rev. Rul. 69-643; *Muskat v. United States*, 554 F.3d 183 (1st Cir. 2009)
